posts.name: Nepycros
posts.cooked:
Same as Lupus, it was dragged out much longer than I anticipated. I had to spend so much time dealing with his trinkets and cultists that by the time he was flipped, all Heroes were under 10 HP. I lasted a few rounds with him by reducing/negating his damage, but eventually he overpowered Skyscraper and Wraith. By the end of the game, I had to use Wraith's Inventory Barrage on all but 2 equipment to sink him down JUST BARELY ENOUGH that a Portal Fiend saw him as the target, and mind-blasted him enough that his own AOE damage destroyed himself.

 

Turns out that once he's flipped, the most important thing to do is to get Visionary in her Cocoon. At the very least, even if Tachyon went down, Visionary would remain. After that, it would be a question of how long until Skinwalker eventually destroyed himself with persistent damage effects. After all, he can only play so many targets to heal up.

posts.cooked:
Comfortable Mint for me

The main driver for my victory was: I gambled on using SST's power on Wraith on the first turn that paid off BIG.  I'll put what I found at the bottom of this post.

Judicious usage of Hypersonic Assault, Throat Jab and Monolith all helped, too.  I finished with everyone near 10, with Wraith doing 19 or so damage on an Inventoy Barrage. 

 

 

 

 

 

 

The bottom of Wraith's deck begins with a Trust Fund and an Impromptu Invention.  Starting her turn with a Razor Ordinace (from Impromptu Invention) and a Combat Stance (From the free play from impromptu invention) really helped.  That Combat Stance went off so many times.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Finished with all heroes in single digits.  Same story as others, mostly.  Throat Jabs, Hypersonic Assaults, and Thorathian Monoliths were pretty key. I used an Infrared Eyepice, coupled with Dark Visionary's various ways to manipulate decks so that neither Gloomweaver's cards nor the environment was too pesky. Lots of pins and zombies and Aggressively Modulated  Explosive Bubbles.

 

At the end, a Lightspeed Barrage left Gloomweaver with 1HP -- so that Dark Visionary was able to lock in the win via Demoralization.

 

I guess Gloomweaver ate so much that he felt he had to give up!

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
Easy Mint. I've gotten Mint on 3 out of the 4 one-shots that have happened since I got the game (as soon as it was available on Mobile) and started paying attention to them. The only one I've gotten Near Mint on was Harbinger of Melancholy, because I revealed the drugs from left to right the first time. The second time, I went 1-3-5, and then he flipped, so I never saw his +1 damage drug or the mill/toxic damage one. He was much easier then.

 

The other 3 -- Freedom Isn't Free, Ghost of Christmas Past, and Nightmare Walking -- went down like chumps. By now I've completed almost all of them, including Desperate Measures, Picnic Interrupted, This Way Madness Lies, Target Rich Environment, and Elementalist. If the game were out in time, I would have gotten Mint or Near Mint on most of them. (Including Desperate Measures; that one was surprisingly not as hard as I would have thought.)

The only ones I haven't completed yet are Advanced Wrath of the Thorathian, Rescue Under the Sea, Frontier Justice, When It Rains, True Heroes of Destiny, and Ridiculous Challenge Time.  Any advice on those?

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
McBehrer:

The only ones I haven't completed yet are Advanced Wrath of the Thorathian, Rescue Under the Sea, Frontier Justice, When It Rains, True Heroes of Destiny, and Ridiculous Challenge Time.  Any advice on those?

Oh cool, some of those go back quite a ways.  I'd love to help with these, it's been months since I've tried several of them.

Ridiculous Challenge Time's thread is still alive on Steam, you might want to check those forums for thoughts.  In general, The Contract is the worst, Hairtrigger Reflexes and Driving Mantis can be your best friends, and don't feel bad if you have a lot of trouble with it.  Not a whole lot of people were able to complete that one.  A couple people did manage to mint it, but most who finished were like me and took 20+ tries to get it done.  On the Sentinels Live stream, I think they said the win rate on that game was under 1%.

When It Rains starts rough, but it gets easier if you leave the Gene-Bound Firesworn alive and try to keep Absolute Zero at the highest HP.  Eventually, Voss's deck slows down, Adhesive Foam Grenade becomes your best friend, you get Cleansing Downpour out, and you get time to set up to nuke Voss.  If you can keep everyone alive after they get down into single-digits, it's easily possible to build up powerful attacks to one-round KO Voss and have everyone back up into the 20s.  

I remember that I abused the crap out of the environment in "Rescue" Under the Sea, to the point where I think the Krakens did as much damage to villains as I did, but I'd have to play it again to remember how I did it.  I'll be back with more thoughts on these later, or you can drop me a message if you like.
